title: History Unit 6: Internal Developments & State Formation
content:
ሰላም የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 👋 እንኳን ወደ History of Ethiopia and the Horn ምዕራፍ 6 (ክፍል 1) በሰላም መጣችሁ! የጥናት ስሜታችሁ ሞቅ እንዳለ ተስፋ አደርጋለሁ። ይህ ምዕራፍ ከ1800 እስከ 1941 በኢትዮጵያ እና በአፍሪካ ቀንድ የነበሩትን የውስጥ እድገቶች፣ የንግድ መስመሮች እና ዘመናዊቷን ኢትዮጵያ የመመስረት ሂደት (State Formation) በጥልቀት ይዳስሳል። ሌላ ምንም አይነት ተጨማሪ ማጣቀሻ (Resource) ሳያስፈልጋችሁ ለፈተና 100% ዝግጁ እንድትሆኑ አድርገን፣ እያንዳንዱን የሞጁል ሀሳብ ከመስመር መስመር አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። እንግዲህ ፈገግ እያልን፣ እያጠናን ታሪካችንን አብረን እንመርምር! 🚀🔥


6.1. Nature of Interactions among the Peoples and States of Ethiopia and the Horn

6.1.1. Peoples and States in South-Central, Southwestern, and Western Ethiopia

A. South-Central: The Qabena State
During the second half of the 19th century, the Qabena state emerged in south-central Ethiopia (northeast of the Gibe River). It was formed through a strong coalition between the Hadiya and Gurage peoples. Notably, Qabena became a powerful political and religious center, particularly as a hub for the Muslim revivalist movement. This movement was significantly fueled by Muslim refugees from Wollo and strong ideological ties with the Mahdist state in Sudan. Under the leadership of Hasan Enjamo, the state fiercely expanded Islamic teachings and resisted external conquests until it was eventually defeated by Menilek's forces (Ras Gobana) in the late 1880s.

B. Southwestern: The Five Gibe States
In the early 19th century, a major political transformation occurred among the Mecha Oromo in the Gibe region. The traditional, democratic Gadaa system began to decline, giving way to monarchical state structures. How did this happen? War leaders (known as Abba-Dulas or Motis) started controlling the lucrative long-distance trade routes. By taxing this trade, they accumulated massive wealth, built private armies, and established hereditary rule.

The five states were:
1. Limmu-Enarya: The earliest Gibe state. Powerful Abba Dulas like Tesso defeated the former Enarya rulers (Badancho, Gu'amcho, Banaro). State formation was solidified by Bofo/Abba Gomol (r. 1800–1825). His son, Ibsa/Abba Bogibo (r. 1825–1861), took over and brought the kingdom to its absolute zenith, incorporating regions like Hagalo and Badi-Folla.
2. Guma: Initiated by Jilcha Abba Bal'o of Chira, who killed Sarbaroda of the Dagoye clan. His son, Oncho (r. 1810–1830), completed the state's formation.
3. Gomma: Formed by Abba Boke (r. 1800–1829). It was heavily influenced by Muslim scholars (ulama), making Gomma the first among the Gibe states to fully embrace Islam.
4. Jimma: Started taking shape in the 18th century under Makahore (an influential woman). It was completed under Sanna / Abba Jifar I (r. 1830–1855). The state became immensely prosperous and famous under Abba Jifar II (r. 1875–1934). Jimma was also an industrial hub, with iron mining at Dakkano and smelting at Kitto.
5. Gera: State formation was completed under Tullu Gunji (r. 1835–1838) and continued by Abba Rago I.

Administrative Structure of Gibe States:
They developed a highly structured bureaucracy:
• Abba Gurmu: Next in rank to the king.
• Abba Mizan: Treasurer/Minister of Foreign Affairs.
• Abba Dango: Chief of Immigration/Borders.
• Lammi: Envoy/Ambassador.
• Abba Qoro: District governor.
• Abba Ganda: Village chief.
• Abba Busi: Tax collector.
• Abba Jiga: Judge for murder cases.
• Abba-Qawe: King's bodyguard (literally 'father of the gun').
Taxes: Unlike the Gadaa system, farmers paid agricultural taxes measured in buchano (approx. 15 kg) and later guboo (25 kg).

C. Western Ethiopia: The Leqa States & Nilotic Sheikdoms
• Leqa-Naqamte: Founded by Bakare Godana in 1840, reached its height under Kumsa Moroda (Dejjach Gebre-Egzi'abiher), who actively promoted gold washing, coffee planting, handcrafts, and trade.
• Leqa-Qellam: Founded by Tullu, expanded under his son Jote, centered at Gidami.
• Ilu: Founded by Chali Shono (Abba Bor) of the Tume clan.
• Nilotic Sheikdoms (Watawit): Formed when Arabic-speaking Sudanese merchants integrated with the indigenous Berta people. Major sheikdoms included Asosa (Aqoldi), Bela/Beni-Shangul, Khomosha, and Guba. Their economy relied heavily on border trade, agriculture, and rich gold mining—which constantly attracted Egyptian and Mahdist invasions.

👉
በ19ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን በደቡብ እና ምዕራብ ኢትዮጵያ ትልልቅ ለውጦች ተከስተዋል።
• ቀበና (Qabena): በሐዲያ እና ጉራጌ ጥምረት የተመሰረተ ሲሆን፣ የእስልምና ሀይማኖት ማስፋፊያ (Muslim revivalist movement) ዋና ማዕከል ነበር። (💡 የሀይማኖቱ መስፋፋት ምክንያት ከወሎ በመጡ ስደተኞች እና ከሱዳን ማህዲስቶች ጋር በነበራቸው ግንኙነት ነው።)
• አምስቱ የጊቤ መንግስታት (Five Gibe States): የኦሮሞ ማህበረሰብ መጀመሪያ በገዳ ስርዓት (Gadaa system) ይተዳደር ነበር። ነገር ግን ንግድ ሲስፋፋ የጦር መሪዎቹ (አባ ዱላዎች) የንግድ መስመሩን ተቆጣጠሩ፣ ሀብት አከማቹ፣ የራሳቸውን ጦር አደራጁ። ከዚያስ? "ዲሞክራሲው ይቆየን፣ እኔው በዘር ማንዘሬ ልምራችሁ" ብለው ወደ ንጉሳዊ (Monarchical) አስተዳደር ቀየሩት። 😂 (ብር እና ስልጣን ሲገኝ ገዳን ረሱት ማለት ነው!)
1. ሊሙ-ኤናርያ: የመጀመሪያው መንግስት ነው። በቦፎ (አባ ጎሞል) ተመስርቶ በልጁ እብሳ (አባ ቦጊቦ) ዘመን እጅግ ጠነከረ።
2. ጉማ: በጅልቻ አባ ባልኦ ተጀምሮ በልጁ ኦንቾ ተጠናቀቀ።
3. ጎማ: በአባ ቦኬ ተመሰረተ። ከሁሉም ቀድሞ እስልምናን የተቀበለ መንግስት ነው።
4. ጅማ: አባ ጅፋር 1ኛ መንግስቱን ሲያጠናክር፣ አባ ጅፋር 2ኛ ደግሞ ታዋቂው እና ጅማን በሀብት ያሳደጋት ንጉስ ነው። ጅማዎች በዳቃኖ የወርቅ... ይቅርታ የብረት ማዕድን (Iron mining) እና በኪቶ የብረት ማቀለጫ (Smelting) ነበራቸው። ዘመናዊ ቴክኖሎጂ ቀድመው ጀምረው ነበር!
5. ጌራ: በቱሉ ጉንጂ ተመሰረተ።
• Exam Hint : የጊቤ ባለስልጣናት ስም ፈተና ላይ አይቀርም። ለምሳሌ Abba Mizan የገንዘብ ሚኒስተር ነው። ሚዛን ማለት መመዘኛ ስለሆነ የሀገሪቱን በጀት 'ይመዝን' ነበር ብላችሁ አስታውሱ! Abba Qawe (የንጉሱ ጠባቂ)፣ Abba Jiga (የነፍስ ግድያ ዳኛ) እነዚህን በደንብ ያዙ።
• የለቃ መንግስታት: ለቃ ነቀምቴ በባካሬ ጎዳና እና በልጁ ኩምሳ ሞሮዳ በጣም ጎልብቶ ነበር።
• የኒሎቲክ ሸይክዶሞች (ወታዊት): ሱዳናውያን ነጋዴዎች ከሀገር በቀሉ የ'በርታ' ህዝብ ጋር ተቀላቅለው የመሰረቷቸው (አሶሳ፣ ቤኒሻንጉል፣ ኮሞሻ) ናቸው። በወርቅ ሀብት ስለበለፀጉ ግብፆች እና የሱዳን ማህዲስቶች ሁሌ ይቋምጡባቸው ነበር።


6.1.2. Trade and Trade Routes

During the 19th century, long-distance trade was the backbone of state formation and urbanization. Two major trade routes linked the resource-rich southwestern regions to external markets.

1. The Southwestern to Northern Route:
Originating from Bonga (Kafa) ➔ Hirmata (Jimma) ➔ Saqa (Limmu) ➔ Billo (Leqa-Naqamte) ➔ Asendabo (Guduru) ➔ Basso-Yajube (Gojjam) ➔ Yifag & Darita (Begemdir) ➔ Gondar.
From Gondar, the route split into two:
• Westward via Chilga to Matamma-Qallabat (Sudan border).
• Northward via Adwa and Asmara to Massawa (Red Sea coast).
*(Another branch from Basso went east through Wollo and Awusa to Djibouti's ports like Tajura and Obbok).*

2. The Southwestern to Eastern Route:
Bonga ➔ Hirmata ➔ Agabja-Andode-Toli-Soddo ➔ Rogge (near Mount Yerer) ➔ Aliyu Amba / Abdul Rasul (major markets in Shewa) ➔ Harar. From Harar, goods went to Somali coastal ports of Zeila and Berbera.

Trade Items & Mediums of Exchange:
• Exports: Civet musk, honey wax, coffee, spices, gold, ivory, and heavily, slaves.
• Imports: Mirrors, ironware, beads, and firearms.
• Mediums of Exchange: Before modern currency, trade relied on barter and specific items:
- Amole (Salt bar): Mined in the Taltal plains of Afar. It was highly regulated. The governor of Enderte in Mekelle held the title Balgada (the official who controlled the salt caravan and collected taxes).
- Maria Theresa Thalers (MTT): An Austrian silver coin bearing the image of Queen Maria Theresa, introduced to the Horn in the late 18th century.
- Cowrie shells and Abujadi (cotton cloth).

Prominent Merchant Groups:
• Afqala: Indigenous Oromo Muslim merchants from the southwest.
• Jabarti: Muslim merchants from the northern provinces.
• Jallaba: Sudanese merchants operating along the borders.
• Argobba: Merchants dominating the route from Shewa to Harar.

👉
ንግድ በ19ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን ለሀገራት መፈጠር ትልቅ ሚና ነበረው። ዋና ዋናዎቹ የንግድ መስመሮች ሁለት ነበሩ፡
1. ወደ ሰሜን የሚያመራው፡ መነሻውን ደቡብ ምዕራብ (ቦንጋ/ጅማ) አድርጎ በጎጃም (ባሶ) አቋርጦ ጎንደር ይደርሳል። ከጎንደር ወደ መተማ (ሱዳን) እና ወደ ምፅዋ (ቀይ ባህር) ይከፈላል።
2. ወደ ምስራቅ የሚያመራው፡ ከደቡብ ምዕራብ ተነስቶ ሸዋ (አሊዩ አምባ) በኩል አድርጎ ሐረር፣ በመጨረሻም ዘይላ እና በርበራ ወደብ ይደርሳል።
• የመገበያያ ገንዘቦች: አሞሌ (ጨው)፣ ማሪያ ቴሬዛ (የኦስትሪያ ብር)፣ የጥጥ ልብስ (አቡጀዲ) ነበሩ።
(😂 አስቡት እስኪ! አሞሌ ጨው እንደ ብር ያገለግል ነበር። ዛሬ ላይ ኪሳችሁ ተቀዶ ብራችሁ ቢወድቅ 'አፈር ሆነ' ይባላል፣ ያኔ ግን አሞሌው መሬት ከወደቀ አጥቦ ለወጥ ማባያ ማድረግ ይቻል ነበር! ፈንጠዝያ ነው!) የአሞሌ ንግዱን እና ግብሩን የሚቆጣጠረው የመቀሌው አስተዳዳሪ 'በልጋዳ' (Balgada) የሚል ማዕረግ ነበረው።
• Exam Hint: ነጋዴዎቹን በደንብ ለዩ! Afqala (የኦሮሞ ሙስሊም ነጋዴዎች)፣ Jabarti (የሰሜን ሙስሊም ነጋዴዎች)፣ እና Jallaba (የሱዳን ነጋዴዎች)።


6.2. The Making of the Modern Ethiopian State (1855-1941)

The modern Ethiopian state formation marked the end of the chaotic Zemene Mesafint (Era of the Princes) and the beginning of political centralization and territorial expansion.

1. Emperor Tewodros II (r. 1855–1868)
Born Kasa Hailu in Qwara, he started as a shifta (bandit/rebel) after being alienated by Ras Ali II and Etege Manan. His primary goal was absolute centralization (one king, one army). To become Emperor, Kasa fought four decisive battles in strict chronological order:
1. Battle of Gur Amba (Nov 27, 1852): Defeated Dejjach Goshu Zewde of Gojjam.
2. Battle of Taqusa (Apr 12, 1853): Defeated four dejjazmachs of Ras Ali (Birru Aligaz, Aben, Yazew, Belew).
3. Battle of Ayshal (Jun 29, 1853): Defeated Ras Ali II. (This officially ended the Zemene Mesafint!)
4. Battle of Deresge (Feb 8, 1855): Defeated Dejjach Wube of Simen and Tigray.
Kasa was crowned Emperor Tewodros II by Abune Salama at Deresge Mariam. However, his harsh centralized policies led to internal rebellions. After imprisoning European missionaries and diplomats, a British expedition led by Sir Robert Napier attacked Maqdela. To avoid capture, Tewodros committed suicide on April 13, 1868.

2. Emperor Tekle-Giorgis II (r. 1868–1871)
Formerly Wagshum Gobaze of Lasta. His reign was short. He was defeated by Kasa Mircha of Tigray at the Battle of Assam (Adwa) in July 1871.

3. Emperor Yohannes IV (r. 1872–1889)
Crowned in 1872, Yohannes (Kasa Mircha) learned from Tewodros's mistakes. He adopted a decentralized administrative approach, allowing regional lords to rule their areas as long as they recognized his absolute suzerainty.
• Liche Agreement (1878): He recognized Menilek as the Negus (King) of Shewa.
• In 1881, he designated Ras Adal Tesema as Negus Tekle-Haymanot of Gojjam and Kafa.
• Council of Boru Meda (1878): Yohannes declared the Tewahedo sect as the only state religion, forcing major Wollo Muslim leaders to convert to Christianity (e.g., Mohammed Ali became Ras Michael).
He died defending Ethiopia against the Mahdists at the Battle of Metemma on March 9, 1889.

4. Emperor Menilek II (r. 1889–1913) - Territorial Expansion
Menilek was the architect of Ethiopia's present-day borders. His expansion had three phases: when he was King of Shewa (1865-89), from his coronation to Adwa (1889-96), and post-Adwa (1896-1900). He used both peaceful diplomacy and armed conquest.
• Peaceful Submissions: Northern Gurage (Kistane), Leqa-Naqamte, Leqa-Qellam, and Jimma Abba Jifar submitted without bloodshed.
• Armed Resistances:
- Gojjam Rivalry: Menilek's Shewan forces defeated Negus Tekle-Haymanot's Gojjam forces at the historic Battle of Embabo (June 6, 1882), giving Menilek control over the rich southwest.
- Arsi Oromo: Fiercely resisted Menilek's army in six campaigns. Despite early victories at Dodota and Qal'ata, Arsi forces were ultimately crushed by Ras Darge at the Battle of Azule (Sept 6, 1886), leading to the tragic Anole incident.
- Harar: Dejjach Mekonnen defeated Emir Abdullahi at the Battle of Chalanqo (Jan 6, 1887), incorporating the vital eastern trade hub.
- Southern Kingdoms: Wolayta resisted fiercely but King (Kawo) Tona was defeated in 1894. Kafa's king, Tato Gaki Sherocho, fought hard but was defeated by Ras Wolde Giorgis in 1897.

5. Emperor Haile-Selassie I (1930-1974) - Post-1900 Centralization
Haile-Selassie successfully completed the centralization process by systematically destroying the regional autonomies created by Yohannes and Menilek. He centralized power by military force, defeating internal rivals (e.g., Nigus Mika'el at the Battle of Segele in 1916, Ras Gugsa Wole at the Battle of Anchim in 1930, and detaining Ras Hailu of Gojjam in 1932).

ይህ ክፍል እንዴት ዘመናዊቷ ኢትዮጵያ እንደተመሰረተች ያሳያል።
• አፄ ቴዎድሮስ 2ኛ: ዘመነ መሳፍንትን በማብቃት ማዕከላዊ አስተዳደር (Centralized state) ጀመሩ። አፄ ከመሆናቸው በፊት ያደረጉትን 4 ጦርነቶች በቅደም ተከተል ለመያዝ GTA-D ብላችሁ አስቡት! 🎮
G = Gur Amba (ጉር አምባ - ደጃች ጎሹን አሸነፉ)
T = Taqusa (ጣቁሳ - የራስ አሊን 4 ጦር መሪዎች አሸነፉ)
A = Ayshal (አይሻል - ራስ አሊን በማሸነፍ ዘመነ መሳፍንትን ቋጩ)
D = Deresge (ደሬስጌ - ደጃች ውቤን አሸንፈው ዘውድ ጫኑ)
ልክ እንደ ጌም (GTA) ቴዎድሮስም ሌቭል እያለፉ ሄደው አፄ ሆኑ ማለት ነው!
• አፄ ዮሐንስ 4ኛ: የቴዎድሮስን ስህተት ተምረው ያልተማከለ (Decentralized) አስተዳደር ነው የተከተሉት። 'እኔ ብቻ ልብላ' ሳይሆን 'የየራሳችሁን ግዛት አስተዳድሩ፣ ግን ለእኔ ግብር ክፈሉ' የሚል ፖሊሲ ነበራቸው። በቦሩ ሜዳ ጉባኤም እስልምናን በማስገደድ የወሎ መሪዎችን አጠመቁ።
• አፄ ምኒልክ 2ኛ: የኢትዮጵያን ካርታ ያስፋፉት እሳቸው ናቸው። አንዳንዶቹ ሀገራት (እንደ ጅማ አባ ጅፋር እና ኪስታኔ ጉራጌ) በሰላም ሲገብሩ፣ አንዳንዶቹ ላይ ጦርነት ተካሂዷል።
- እምባቦ ጦርነት (1882): ሸዋ እና ጎጃም ደቡብ ምዕራብን ለመቆጣጠር ያደረጉት ወሳኝ ጦርነት።
- አዙሌ ጦርነት (1886): የአርሲ ኦሮሞዎች ጠንካራ ተቃውሞ ሲያደርጉ ቆይተው በራስ ዳርጌ የተሸነፉበት።
- ጨለንቆ ጦርነት (1887): ደጃች መኮንን የሐረርን ኤሚር አብዱላሂን ያሸነፉበት።
• አፄ ኃይለሥላሴ: እነዚህን የክልል ገዢዎች ኃይል በመስበር ሙሉ በሙሉ ሀገሪቱን በማዕከላዊነት (Centralization) ጠቀለሉ።
